info.name: Waste Submit Reg Packaging API
info.description:
Requests for waste-submit-reg-packaging-api: aggregated packaging data for the Obligations service.

**Two endpoints**

- `GET /packaging/{year}/aggregated-submissions`: every approved submission for the year, grouped by submitter.
- `GET /packaging/{year}/organisation/{organisationId}/aggregated-submission`: the organisations for one submitter.

Both return approved submissions only. Each organisation carries its joiner or leaver code (numbered as in the [GOV.UK registration file guidance](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/register-for-epr-for-packaging-create-your-registration-file)), the matching date, and its packaging in tonnes per material.

**Quick start**

1. Run the service: `dotnet run --project WasteSubmitRegPackagingApi` (port 8085).
2. Open **1. Local (stub data)** and send any request, or right-click the folder and choose **Run folder** to run every test.

**Variables** (collection variables, edit on the collection's Variables tab)

- `baseUrl`: the local service.
- `year`: the packaging year. The stub has data for 2024.
- `directRegistrantId`, `complianceSchemeId`: the two submitters in the stub data.
- `cdpBaseUrl`, `cdpApiKey`: for the CDP dev folder.

The service is still serving stub data, so the numbers are examples.

item.name: 2. CDP dev
item.description:
For once the service is deployed to CDP dev. You need:

1. The AWS OpenVPN connected.
2. `cdpApiKey` set to your Developer API key (CDP Portal, your profile). Put it in the **Current value** column so it is not shared if the collection is exported.

A protected-zone service is not reachable directly from a laptop, so these go through the ephemeral-protected endpoint, which gives up after about 5 seconds.
